primitives.name: Growth Gap Identity
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Growth gap:** g_t⋆ - g_t^π = 1⁄2‖θ_t - σ_tTπ_t‖2 — the instantaneous growth shortfall of any portfolio π is half the squared tracking error to the Kelly portfolio in volatility units.

primitives.name: Objective KL Divergence
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Objective identity:** E_P[log(X_T^{π⋆}/X_T^π)] = D_KL(P‖P^π) — expected log-wealth ratio under the true measure equals the KL divergence between the true measure and the measure under which π is growth-optimal.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'true probability measure (dimensionless)', 'P^{\\pi}': 'measure under which π is growth-optimal (dimensionless)', 'X_T^{\\pi}': 'wealth process of portfolio π at time T (dimensionless)', 'D_{KL}': 'Kullback-Leibler divergence (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: True measure P and induced measure P^π are absolutely continuous.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P and P^π are not mutually absolutely continuous.

layer2.mapping: Relates wealth growth to information-theoretic divergence between true and implied measures.
layer2.telemetry: Expected log-wealth ratio under true measure

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that portfolio suboptimality can be precisely quantified using KL divergences. The Kelly condition defines the optimal portfolio via σ_t^T π_t^* = θ_t, linking portfolio weights directly to market risk premiums. The growth gap identity then expresses how far any portfolio π is from optimal in terms of squared deviation in volatility-weighted space. This is further connected to KL divergences: the objective identity equates expected log-wealth difference to KL divergence between true and implied measures, while the subjective identity mirrors this under investor beliefs. These identities form a duality pair, enabling precise measurement of both objective and subjective suboptimality. Failure modes arise when assumptions break—such as non-full rank volatility or non-admissible portfolios—leading to undefined or infinite divergences.
